questions.q: Why does AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL exist as a separate table between AP_INVOICES_ALL and AP_CHECKS_ALL?
options: Because the relationship between invoices and checks isn't one-to-one: an invoice can span multiple checks, and a check can pay multiple invoices
It doesn't serve any real purpose — it's a legacy table
Because AP_CHECKS_ALL cannot be joined directly to any other table
Because Oracle requires every join to involve exactly three tables
questions.explain: A linking table is needed because one invoice can be paid across multiple checks, and one check can pay multiple invoices.

questions.q: In the three-table join (invoices -> invoice_payments -> checks), what does each additional INNER JOIN require?
options: Nothing — only the first join needs an ON condition
Its own ON condition correctly connecting it to an already-joined table
A completely separate SELECT statement
A GROUP BY clause
questions.explain: Each JOIN in a chain needs its own ON predicate connecting the new table into the existing chain of joins.

questions.q: If invoice 5001 was paid by two separate checks, how many rows does the three-table join (invoices to invoice_payments to checks) return for invoice 5001?
options: Exactly one row, with the two check amounts combined
Zero rows, because of the ambiguity
Two rows — one per check, reflecting what actually happened
An error, since one invoice cannot have two payments
questions.explain: The join returns one row per invoice-to-check relationship, so two checks produce two rows for that invoice.

questions.q: Which table tracks what's still owed on an invoice (due date, amount remaining), independent of whether a check has been cut yet?
options: AP_CHECKS_ALL
AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL
POZ_SUPPLIERS
AP_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL
questions.explain: AP_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL tracks DUE_DATE and AMOUNT_REMAINING, which is the outstanding-balance source for unpaid-invoice questions.

questions.q: What does `ip.amount AS amount_on_this_check` return in the three-table join?
options: The total invoice amount, regardless of how many checks paid it
The portion of the invoice amount paid by this specific check
The remaining unpaid balance on the invoice
The supplier's total outstanding balance across all invoices
questions.explain: AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL.AMOUNT records the amount applied to the invoice by that specific check — not the full invoice total.
